newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU and S.Africa sign research cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: EU and S.Africa sign research cooperation pact.

text.p: The European Union and South Africa signed a cooperation pact on Thursday allowing their researchers to take part in joint projects.
The move will allow South African researchers to cooperate with those in the EU on projects agreed within the bloc's current, 13-billion-European-currency-unit research programme from 1994 to 1998.

"This agreement will provide a framework for further developing cooperation between the (European Union) and South Africa in fields of common interest where they are supporting research and development, including demonstration activities to advance science and technology," said a statement released at the signing ceremony.
The deal does not provide South Africans with any new research money as such but does open the way for their involvement and possible funding via EU aid programmes.
Similarly, EU scientists may now take part in South African research projects, shared use of facilities, seminars, workshops, data exchange and training.
The accord was based on the draft decision on the science and technology agreement with South Africa, as detailed in proposal COM(96)423.
